name: ejs-angularjs-navigator
description: Tracks variables/functions between EJS templates and AngularJS 1.x controllers

commands.title: EJS/NG: Log This Variable at Runtime

ejsng.include.description: Glob patterns for files to index.

ejsng.moduleAliases.description: Variable names treated as an Angular module when no angular.module() declaration is found in the same file.

urlPrefix.description: URL prefix as written in templateUrl, e.g. "/views/".

fsPath.description: Directory it is served from, relative to the workspace root, e.g. "src/views".

extensions.description: Extensions to try when the file behind the URL has a different one, e.g. [".ejs", ".html"].

ejsng.templateRoots.description: Maps runtime templateUrl values (directive, component, $routeProvider, $stateProvider) to template files, so a template's expressions resolve against the controller that renders it. Reload the window after changing.

ejsng.expressViewsDir.description: Express views directory, relative to the workspace root — where res.render('user/profile') looks for its view. Reload the window after changing.

ejsng.diagnostics.enabled.description: Enables warnings for variables that don't exist on scope. Defaults to OFF to avoid false positives on legacy code.

ejsng.typeHints.nullable.description: Shows a faint "may be empty" hint after a template variable that is explicitly assigned null or undefined somewhere in its controller — an Angular expression renders empty then, it doesn't throw. The full observed type is always on hover. Reload the window after changing.

ejsng.runtimeLog.pathMappings.description: Maps a container-internal path to its path on this machine, for inline runtime log from a Dockerized process (e.g. [{"remote": "/app", "local": "/Users/me/project"}]). Usually not needed: mappings are inferred from the connected container's own mounts. Declare one here to override that, or for a process this extension can't read the mounts of. Not needed at all for a process running directly on this machine. Under Remote-WSL, write Linux paths (/home/me/project); a pasted \\wsl.localhost\… path is read as its Linux path. The most specific remote is applied first, whatever the order here.

remote.description: Path prefix as reported by the container, e.g. /app

local.description: The matching path on this machine, e.g. /Users/me/project. May use ${workspaceFolder} so the mapping can be committed to the repo.

ejsng.runtimeLog.chromeExecutablePath.markdownDescription:
Browser executable used by the panel's **Launch browser** button. Empty = find one on your machine: Chrome, then Edge, then Brave (on Windows, the registry first, then the usual install folders). When set, this path always wins.

Under Remote-WSL the browser runs on Windows: a Windows path such as `C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe` works.

ejsng.runtimeLog.chromeDebugPort.description: --remote-debugging-port the panel's 'Launch browser' button starts the browser with, and connects to.

ejsng.runtimeLog.logpoints.markdownDescription: Show VS Code **logpoints** inline while connected to a runtime (right-click the gutter → *Add Logpoint…*, e.g. `user = {user.name}`). The extension sets them on the runtime itself, so they work without a VS Code debug session, and never pause the app. Turn off if you are also debugging the same app with VS Code's own debugger and don't want each logpoint twice in the Debug Console.

ejsng.runtimeLog.skipFrames.markdownDescription: Extra glob patterns for stack frames to never anchor a runtime log to (e.g. a vendored logger not already covered by the defaults, or your team's own log wrapper). This ADDS to the built-in default list — it never replaces it. Defaults already skipped: `node:internal/**`, `node:*`, `**/node_modules/**`, and common logger directories (`log4js`, `winston`, `bunyan`, `pino`).
